newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money ends easier, mid-term gilts active.
newsitem.headline: India call money ends easier, mid-term gilts active.

text.p: Indian call money closed lower at 5.75-6.50 percent, off the day's opening levels of 6.75-7.50 percent, dealers said.
"Most of the deals were in the region of 5.75-6.25 percent," a state-run bank dealer said.
"The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s intervention in the foreign exchange market and repayment of the last repo will add over 30 billion rupees to liquidity," he said.
Dealers foresaw rates sliding to 5.0 percent on Saturday.
"Call rates are hovering in the same band with liquidity easy, and there will be positive inflows into the banking system on Saturday," M. Srinivas, a dealer at Centurion Bank said.
Securities yields will fall due to the growing liquidity, Srinivas said.
The securities market was active on Friday, dealers said.
The nationalised bank offloaded their 11.64 percent 2000 security at a price ranging from 99.15 rupees to 99.30 rupees, at a volume of 1.6 billion rupees, dealers said.
The newly auctioned 12.14 percent government stock 2000 dealt at 100.10 rupees, compared to a previous 100.00 rupees, dealers said.
The 12.69 percent 2002 stock rose to 100.45 rupees, against the previous 100.40 rupees, dealers said.
